name: Subharmonic Thermal Vortex Projector STVP-2 'Millstone'
description:
The STVP-2 generates a localized thermal vortex by simultaneously projecting two intersecting subharmonic infrared beams at a target point. Where the beams converge, destructive interference between their waveforms produces a rapidly rotating thermal gradient — a spinning column of alternating hot and cool bands that exerts torsional mechanical stress on any matter caught within it. The effect on organic tissue is visceral: the vortex does not burn so much as it wrings, producing deep-tissue trauma analogous to extreme mechanical torsion while leaving the skin surface comparatively intact. Internal hemorrhaging and structural damage to connective tissue are the primary injury mechanisms.

Zheng-Dao Bioelectric developed the STVP-2 originally as an industrial tool for non-contact material stress-testing, and the weapon's lineage is visible in its form factor — it resembles a modified survey instrument more than a firearm, with a wide dual-emitter head mounted on a pistol-grip frame and a large rotary dial on the side for adjusting vortex intensity and rotation frequency. The 'Millstone' nickname refers both to this dial and to the grinding quality of the effect on targets. Operators describe the sound of a firing weapon as a low, nauseating hum that is felt more than heard.

The weapon's primary limitation is its fixed effective range of 6–14 meters — the intersecting beams require a minimum distance to converge properly and lose coherence beyond the maximum. This makes the Millstone unsuitable for long-range engagements, but within its optimal band it produces injuries that body armor is largely ineffective against, as the torsional effect penetrates most rigid materials by exploiting their own internal stress fracture lines.
specifications:
effective range: 6–14m fixed band
vortex rotation speed: 40–800 RPM adjustable
beam wavelength: Dual-channel, 9.4μm and 10.6μm infrared
power cell: Zheng-Dao ZD-8 cell, 22 charges at max intensity
weight: 4.7kg
dimensions: 58cm length, 21cm width at emitter head
armor penetration: High against rigid plate; moderate against ablative mesh
charge time: 0.8 seconds to full vortex coherence
tactical_use: The Millstone is a close-to-mid-range ambush weapon. Operators typically use it from concealed positions within the 6–14m band, targeting unarmored torsos or limbs. The 0.8-second coherence delay means it performs poorly against highly mobile targets; experienced users pre-aim and trigger the charge before the target enters the optimal zone. The prohibited status means it appears almost exclusively in black market arsenals, used by operators who need to defeat armored targets without the noise signature of kinetic weapons.
cultural_context: The Millstone occupies a notorious place in GLMZ's criminal ecology. Because it leaves minimal external marks on victims — the damage is internal — it has been used in murders that were initially misclassified as medical events. Forensic examiners have developed specific autopsy protocols to identify STVP-2 injuries, but these require specialized equipment that only high-tier coroner's offices possess. In lower districts, Millstone killings frequently go unsolved. The weapon is associated with professional contract killing and organized crime enforcement, rather than street violence.
story_hooks: A series of deaths in a mid-district apartment block are ruled cardiac arrest, but a street-level medic notices the internal injury pattern and recognizes it. Someone is using a Millstone to commit untraceable murders — and the victims all have one thing in common.

Zheng-Dao Bioelectric's official position is that no STVP-2 units were ever converted to weapons — they are all survey instruments. But a player character finds one with a Zheng-Dao military-grade power cell that doesn't exist in any public product catalog.

A black market arms dealer is selling Millstones in bulk — far more units than any one workshop could produce. Either a Zheng-Dao production line has been compromised, or someone has reverse-engineered the design at scale.
